# Your first entity

This tutorial walks the entity model end to end — the shapes the
substrate moves, before any binary exists to drive them. Everything
here is the wire contract `hypha-node-api` already implements.

## The three primitives

**Entity** — the thing being orchestrated:

```json
{
  "id": "sess-42",
  "kind": "sepia-session",
  "node": "node-a",
  "indexDoc": { "title": "fix the flaky test", "locked": false },
  "health": { "live": true }
}
```

`kind` is a free-form tag registered by an integration.
`indexDoc` is opaque JSON the integration writes for list views —
hypha stores and merges it, never interprets it.

**Op** — a command submitted to an entity's owner node:

```json
{ "entity": "sess-42", "kind": "sepia.prompt", "payload": { "text": "hi" } }
```

Op kinds are namespaced `<integration>.<verb>`; payloads are opaque
to hypha. `entity.delete` is the one reserved substrate op.

**Snapshot** — serialize → transfer → resume:

```json
{ "entity": "sess-42", "ref": "…", "bytes": "…" }
```

Bytes are opaque end-to-end; export/import semantics belong to the
integration that owns the kind.

## The flow

1. A client (CLI, hub, another integration) lists entities:
   `GET /api/entities` → merged index rows `{id, kind, indexDoc, …}`.
2. It submits an op: `POST /api/entities/{id}/ops`. If the owner node
   is down, the hub's `hypha-outbox` queues it per-entity FIFO and
   replays on reconnect.
3. Before routing, `hypha-control` arbitrates: is the entity locked,
   who owns it, does this op preempt or queue?
4. To move a workload: `GET …/snapshot` on the owner, `POST
   /api/entities/snapshot` on the target — the integration's
   export/import does the rest.

## Try it in code

`hypha-node-api` ships `FakeEntityApi` — an in-memory `EntityApi`
impl for tests — and `HttpEntityApi`, the ureq client for real
nodes. `hypha-control`'s `pick_owner`/`Arbitration` are pure functions
you can exercise without any I/O.

```rust
use hypha_control::{pick_owner, Arbitration};
```

See [reference/crates](../reference/crates.md) for the full surface.

# Build and test

```bash
cargo xtask check     # cargo fmt --check + clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings
cargo xtask test      # cargo nextest run --workspace (falls back to cargo test)
cargo xtask coverage  # cargo llvm-cov HTML report → target/llvm-cov/html
cargo xtask fmt       # apply formatting
```

CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs lint, nextest + doctests, and a
coverage job that **gates on 100% line coverage** — any `DA:<line>,0`
in the lcov report fails the build.

Scope a single crate while iterating:

```bash
cargo nextest run -p hypha-outbox
cargo clippy -p hypha-control --all-targets
```

# Read the ledger

All project state lives in the `project/` worktree via
[myco](https://github.com/9aia/myco) — tasks, backlog, issues,
proposals, plans, ADRs, handoffs. Never hand-edit files there; the
`myco` verbs are the write path.

```bash
myco status --prompt   # the board, token-sized
myco resume PL-005     # the extraction plan — briefing + handoffs
myco view board        # kanban
```

The master plan for this repo's existence is **PL-005** in the org
ledger (`9aia/workspace → repos/project`): "hypha — entity substrate
extraction from peregrin". Its handoffs carry the phase-by-phase
execution log.

# Architecture

Hypha is the *substrate* layer: distributed primitives over generic
entities. It owns who may act on an entity, when, and on which
machine — plus the transport that gets ops and snapshots there.

```
                 ┌─────────────── hypha-hub ───────────────┐
                 │  merged index · op routing · push · SSE  │
                 └──────────────┬───────────────┬──────────┘
                        HTTP+SSE │               │ HTTP+SSE
                  ┌──────────────▼──┐    ┌───────▼──────────┐
                  │ hypha node A    │    │ hypha node B     │
                  │ /api/entities*  │    │ /api/entities*   │
                  │ KindRegistry    │    │ KindRegistry     │
                  └───────┬─────────┘    └────────┬─────────┘
                          │  integrations register entity planes:
              ┌───────────┼───────────────────────┼───────────┐
              ▼           ▼                       ▼           ▼
        sepia-session  campaign-run          <kind-N>     entity.*
        (sepia repo)   (peregrin repo)       (any repo)   (substrate)
```

## Planes

* **Entity plane** — this repo: `EntityApi` contract
  (`hypha-node-api`), node host (`hypha serve`, `hypha-node` +
  `hypha-http`), hub gateway (`hypha-hub`), projection
  (`hypha-sync`), outbox (`hypha-outbox`), arbitration
  (`hypha-control`), push.
* **Integration planes** — one per workload kind, living in the
  workload's own repo: `sepia-peregrin` (sepia repo) registers
  `kind="sepia-session"`; peregrin registers `kind="campaign"`.
  An integration translates entity ops ↔ its verbs and implements
  snapshot as its own serialize/resume.
* **Orchestration plane** — campaigns, drivers, loaders. Stays in
  peregrin; becomes a *workload on* hypha rather than a peer of it.

## Ports and adapters

Every I/O seam is a port (`hypha-secret`, `hypha-service`, …) with
impls behind it (`-keyring`, `-dotenv`, `-systemd`). The substrate
contracts are pure — `hypha-control` has no I/O at all.

## Dataflow

Client → hub `POST /api/entities/{id}/ops` → lock gate
(`hypha-control`) → owner node `POST /api/entities/{id}/ops` → the
kind's `EntityPlane::op`. Node down? `hypha-outbox` FIFO per entity,
replayed oldest-first on reconnect. Reads merge through
`hypha-sync`'s SQLite projection + SSE diff tail.

---

---
url: /hypha/explanation/model.md
---
# Entities, ops, snapshots

The whole substrate is three primitives. Get these and the rest is
plumbing.

## Entity

`{id, kind, node, indexDoc, health}`

* `kind` — free-form tag; the integration's namespace
  (`sepia-session`, `campaign`, …).
* `indexDoc` — opaque JSON for list views. Hypha merges and
  columnizes it; meaning belongs to the integration.
* `health` — liveness/lock state reported by the owner node.

## Op

`{entity, kind, payload}` — submitted to an entity's **owner node**.

* `kind` is namespaced `<integration>.<verb>` (`sepia.prompt`,
  `campaign.start`); `entity.*` is the reserved substrate namespace
  (`entity.delete` only, today).
* `payload` is opaque to hypha — the owning plane interprets it.
* Ops are idempotent-keyed and TTL'd in the outbox; `Turn`-class ops
  dead-letter on first failure.

## Snapshot

`{entity, ref, bytes}` — the migration primitive.

Serialize on the owner (`GET /api/entities/{id}/snapshot`), import on
the target (`POST /api/entities/snapshot`). Bytes are opaque
end-to-end; resume semantics are the integration's
(`campaign-snapshot/v1`, sepia session IR export, …).

## Why generic

The distributed abilities — sync, arbitration, outbox, transfer,
pairing — are orchestration-domain but workload-agnostic. Shaping
them around sessions was the mistake ADR-0091 corrected; shaping
them around *entities* is what lets bupha jobs, sturn claims, or
cicada schedules become kinds without touching this repo.

---

---
url: /hypha/explanation/boundary.md
---
# Boundary with sepia and peregrin

Hypha sits between two neighbors and must stay generic against both.

## sepia — session *mechanism*

Sepia owns everything you can do **to** a session: attach, prompt,
restore, rewind, per-agent stores. It is deliberately just the
agent-session abstraction — it must never learn about locks,
multi-node, or orchestration.

Hypha's side of the contract: the `sepia-peregrin` adapter (which
lives **in the sepia repo**) registers `kind="sepia-session"`
entities, translates entity ops ↔ session verbs, and implements
snapshot as sepia's session IR export/import. Hypha never names a
sepia type; sepia never learns hypha exists — the adapter is the
only coupling, and it depends on hypha's public API, never the
reverse.

## peregrin — orchestration *policy + campaigns*

Peregrin owns campaigns (declarative event-driven workflows),
drivers, loaders, and policy (who may act, when, from where). Post
PL-005, peregrin's distributed layer **is** hypha: `peregrin-node`
becomes a thin composition root that registers entity planes —
`sepia-session` (via the adapter) and `campaign` (its own
`campaign_entity.rs`) — on a hypha node host.

The dependency direction is one-way:

```
peregrin (orchestration) → hypha (substrate) → ports
```

Orchestration may sit *on* the substrate; the substrate never
imports orchestration. `peregrin-hub`'s gateway role moves to
`hypha-hub`; peregrin keeps campaign verbs in its CLI.

## The rule of thumb

* "Something you do to a workload" → the integration repo.
* "Who may act on entity X, when, from where" → hypha.
* "A workflow of events and steps" → peregrin.

---
url: /hypha/reference/crates.md

# Crates

Rust workspace, ports-and-adapters. Lints are strict (pedantic warn,
`unwrap_used`/`expect_used` warn, `unsafe_code` forbid); edition
2024, rust-version 1.85.

| Crate | Role | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hypha-node-api` | `EntityApi` trait + wire DTOs + `HttpEntityApi`/`FakeEntityApi` | landed |
| `hypha-outbox` | durable per-entity FIFO op queue (SQLite) | landed |
| `hypha-control` | pure arbitration — locks, takeover, `pick_owner` | landed |
| `hypha-telemetry` | opt-in OTEL over `tracing` | landed |
| `hypha-secret` | secrets port (`get`/`set`, names not values) | landed |
| `hypha-keyring` | OS-keyring impl (`secret-tool`) | landed |
| `hypha-dotenv` | dotenv-file impl | landed |
| `hypha-service` | service-install port | landed |
| `hypha-systemd` | systemd unit render/install impl | landed |
| `hypha-sync` | entity-index projection + sync engine (ex-`peregrin-sync`) | landed |
| `hypha-push` | Web Push over a JSON doc store — VAPID, subscriptions, 404/410 prune (ex-`peregrin-push`) | landed |
| `hypha-http` | substrate HTTP surface — `/api/entities*` kind planes, `/api/entity-index`/`/api/pending-ops`, `/api/events` feed, node/pairing/auth, `/api/push/*` (ex-`peregrin-http` split) | landed |
| `hypha-hub` | aggregation gateway (ex-`peregrin-hub`) — `SyncEntityApi`, merged `/api/entities*`, SSE/passthrough proxies, push, node credentials; policy-injected `KindPolicies`; `hypha-hub` bin (`HYPHA_NODES` + `HYPHA_HUB_*` env) | landed |
| `hypha-node` | node host library (`Env`→`HyphaState`→`hypha_http::app`, `with_kind` plane registration) + `hypha` bin (`hypha serve`, zero kinds) | landed |
| `xtask` | `check` (fmt + clippy) / `test` / `coverage` / `fmt` | landed |

Migration state lives in org-ledger plan **PL-005**; crate-level
API docs build via `bun run docs:api` (cargo doc →
`public/api/`).

---
url: /hypha/reference/environment.md

# Environment

Hypha-native variables (landed crates):

| Variable | Crate | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HYPHA_OTEL_ENDPOINT` | `hypha-telemetry` | OTLP base endpoint; `/v1/traces` appended when no path present |
| `HYPHA_OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` | `hypha-telemetry` | service.name (default `"hypha"`, `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` also honored) |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*` | `hypha-telemetry` | standard OTLP vars also enable export |

Standard OTEL vars (`OTEL_*`) are honored per OpenTelemetry semantic
conventions.

Node host (`hypha serve`, `hypha-http::env::Env`):

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `HYPHA_HOST` / `HYPHA_PORT` (or `PORT`) | bind address (default `127.0.0.1:18787`) |
| `HYPHA_TOKEN` | bearer auth; required on non-loopback binds |
| `HYPHA_HOME` | hypha data dir (default `~/.local/share/hypha`) |
| `HYPHA_NODE` | node identity file (default `<home>/node.json`) |
| `HYPHA_NAME` | display name on `GET /api/node` |
| `HYPHA_ORIGINS` | CORS allowlist |
| `HYPHA_SSE_KEEPALIVE_MS` | `/api/events` keep-alive cadence (`0` disables) |
| `HYPHA_PAIR_LIMIT_PER_MIN` / `HYPHA_PAIR_LIMIT_PER_DAY` | `/api/pair` throttle per client IP |
| `HYPHA_PUSH` / `HYPHA_PUSH_PATH` | push config document (default `<home>/push.json`) |

Hub (`hypha-hub`, `hypha_hub::HubConfig` + `hub_state_from_with`):

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `HYPHA_HUB_HOST` / `HYPHA_HUB_PORT` (or `HYPHA_PORT`) | bind (default `127.0.0.1:13000`) |
| `HYPHA_HUB_TOKEN` | client→hub auth; required on non-loopback binds |
| `HYPHA_NODE_URL` / `HYPHA_NODE_TOKEN` | single-node upstream shorthand |
| `HYPHA_NODES` | `id=url[@token];…` multi-node registry |
| `HYPHA_HOME` | hub data under `<home>/hub/` (projection, outbox, push, credentials) |
| `HYPHA_CREDENTIAL_STORE` | `auto`/`keyring`/`file` node-token backend |

Both binaries (`hypha serve`, `hypha-hub`) initialize the same OTEL
layer — the `HYPHA_OTEL_*`/`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*` vars above apply to
each process.

---

---
url: /hypha/reference/wire-api.md
---
# Wire API

The entity-plane HTTP surface — served by the node host
(`hypha-http`), aggregated by the hub (`hypha-hub`). One canonical
spelling per route: `hypha-node-api`'s `HttpEntityApi` and the hub
speak the same paths. (The P3-era alias spellings —
`/api/entities/{id}/export`, `/api/entities/import`, `/api/index`,
`/api/outbox` — are gone.)

## Node surface

| Route | Verb | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/api/health` | GET | liveness probe (pre-auth) |
| `/api/pair` | POST | redeem a pairing code → bearer token |
| `/api/auth/login` `/api/auth/logout` | POST | auth-cookie exchange |
| `/api/user` | GET | OS user info for pickers |
| `/api/node` | GET/PATCH | node descriptor / rename |
| `/api/fs?path=` | GET | direct subdirectories of an absolute path |
| `/api/events` | GET | SSE event feed |
| `/api/entities` | GET/POST | list (`?kind=`) / create entity |
| `/api/entities/{id}` | GET/DELETE | entity doc / `entity.delete` |
| `/api/entities/{id}/ops` | POST | submit op `{kind, payload}` |
| `/api/entities/{id}/snapshot` | GET | export snapshot bytes |
| `/api/entities/snapshot` | POST | import snapshot (`body.kind` picks the plane) |
| `/api/entity-index` | GET | `{"index": [{node, entities}]}` — one row, this node |
| `/api/pending-ops` | GET | `{"ops": [...]}` — always empty on a bare node (the outbox is hub-side) |
| `/api/push/vapid` | GET | `{publicKey}` (501 without a push store) |
| `/api/push/subscribe` | POST/DELETE | push subscription add/remove |

## Hub surface

Same `/api/entities*` shape, aggregated: merged index from all
`HYPHA_NODES` nodes, ops routed to the owner (durable outbox when
offline), plus hub-owned routes:

| Route | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `/api/entity-index` | merged per-node entity buckets |
| `/api/pending-ops` | outbox depth — queued + dead-letter ops |
| `/api/events` | SSE bridge to the upstream node |
| `/api/entities/{id}/stream` | per-entity live stream (kind policy's `stream_path`, owning node) |
| `/api/push/*` | hub-owned subscription store (fans out to every node) |
| `/api/{*rest}` | passthrough to the upstream node for everything else |

Not on the substrate: `/api/config*` — node config is
integration-owned (a composing integration mounts its own surface);
`EntityApi::get_config`/`set_config` are doc-hidden for that reason.

## Client

`hypha_node_api::HttpEntityApi` (ureq) implements `EntityApi`;
`FakeEntityApi` is the in-memory test double. Wire DTOs:
`EntityDto`, `EntityOp`, `EntityIndexDto`, `PendingOpDto`,
`NodeInfoDto`, `NodeStatusDto`, `PushSubscriptionDto` — see
`hypha-node-api/src/dto.rs` and the generated rustdoc under
`/hypha/api/`.

---
url: /hypha/getting-started.md
---
# Getting started

Hypha is the distributed substrate extracted from peregrin's entity
plane (org plan PL-005, ADR-0001). It ships two binaries: `hypha`
(the node host, `hypha serve`) and `hypha-hub` (the multi-node
gateway). A bare node mounts zero entity kinds — integrations
register theirs at composition.

## Build from source

```bash
git clone git@github.com:9aia/hypha.git
cd hypha
./scripts/setup.sh      # wires git hooks
cargo xtask check       # fmt + clippy -D warnings
cargo xtask test        # whole suite (nextest if present)
```

Rust 1.98 (see `rust-toolchain.toml`), edition 2024.

## Install the binaries

There is no `xtask install` — install straight from the workspace:

```bash
cargo install --path crates/hypha-node --locked   # → ~/.cargo/bin/hypha
cargo install --path crates/hypha-hub --locked   # → ~/.cargo/bin/hypha-hub
```

## Smoke run

A bare node needs no kinds and no config — loopback binds may go
tokenless:

```bash
hypha serve            # HYPHA_HOST/HYPHA_PORT, default 127.0.0.1:18787
curl localhost:18787/api/health        # {"ok":true}
curl localhost:18787/api/node          # node descriptor
curl localhost:18787/api/entities      # {"entities":[]} — no kinds yet
```

The hub gateways that node (`HYPHA_NODE_URL` defaults to
`http://127.0.0.1:18787`):

```bash
hypha-hub              # HYPHA_HUB_HOST/HYPHA_HUB_PORT, default 127.0.0.1:13000
curl localhost:13000/api/entity-index  # merged index (one row)
curl localhost:13000/api/pending-ops   # outbox depth
```

See [Environment](reference/environment.md) for the full `HYPHA_*`
surface and [Wire API](reference/wire-api.md) for the routes.

## Upgrading from peregrin — secrets move

`hypha-keyring` stores under the `secret-tool` service attribute
`"hypha"` (was `"peregrin"`), and `hypha-hub` node credentials live
under `"hypha-hub"` (was `"peregrin-hub"`). **There is no automatic
migration** — old entries are orphaned, not moved. After upgrading:

* re-run pairing (`POST /api/pair` flow) or re-store secrets with
  `secret-tool store --label "hypha: <name>" service hypha name <name>`
* hub node tokens: either re-pair each node, or let an env
  `HYPHA_NODES` `@token`/`HYPHA_NODE_TOKEN` re-seed the store on the
  next boot (`HYPHA_CREDENTIAL_STORE` picks keyring vs file backend)

## Where next

* [Your first entity](tutorials/first-entity.md) — the entity model
  end to end, with wire shapes.
* [Architecture](explanation/architecture.md) — planes, nodes, hub.
* [Boundary](explanation/boundary.md) — what hypha owns vs sepia and
  peregrin.
